standard_prerequisites.name: Computation of derived Hom by property (I) modules
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies RHom(N, -) with Hom into differential graded B-modules with property (I), the starting point for both the transformation and its quasi-isomorphism analysis.

standard_prerequisites.name: Computing Rlim of filtered Hom systems and Hom into shifted duals
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: More on Algebra, Lemma more-algebra-lemma-compute-Rlim; Same chapter, Lemma lemma-hom-into-shift-dual-free
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets the filtered system of quotients I/F_p I be read through complexes computing Rlim, and finally reduces each graded piece to the dual map on B-duals.

core_obligations: Transformation of functors (proof lines 5302-5315): for I with property (I), composition with f is a map of differential graded A-modules Hom_B(N', I) to Hom_B(N, I), functorial in I; since RHom(N', -) and RHom(N, -) are computed by Hom into property-(I) objects (lemma-derived-restriction), this assembles into the transformation RHom(N', -) to RHom(N, -).

Reduction to filtered pieces (proof lines 5317-5336): with the given filtration F_p I on I and I the limit of I/F_p I, Hom into I is the limit of the Hom systems into I/F_p I; the transition maps are split as graded modules, hence the Hom-system transition maps are surjective, so the Hom complexes compute Rlim of the systems (more-algebra-lemma-compute-Rlim); it suffices to prove each Hom_B(N', I/F_p I) to Hom_B(N, I/F_p I) a quasi-isomorphism.

Induction on the filtration (proof lines 5337-5346): the surjections I/F_{p+1} I to I/F_p I are split as graded B-modules, giving short exact sequences of differential graded A-modules on Hom for N' and for N, and f induces a map between them; by induction from p = 0 (where I/F_0 I = 0) it suffices to handle F_p I / F_{p+1} I.

Dual reduction (proof lines 5347-5351): F_p I / F_{p+1} I is a product of shifts of the B-dual, so by lemma-hom-into-shift-dual-free it suffices that (N')^dual to N^dual is a quasi-isomorphism, which holds because f is a quasi-isomorphism and the dual is an exact functor.
proof_roadmap: Assemble the transformation of functors from the property-(I) computation of derived Hom.
Filter I, pass to the quotients through the Rlim computation, and reduce to the graded pieces.
Induct on the filtration using the split surjections and the induced maps of short exact sequences.
Reduce each graded piece to the dual map via shifts of the B-dual and conclude by exactness of the dual.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves functoriality of derived restriction in the bimodule and that quasi-isomorphisms of bimodules induce isomorphisms of functors (statement lines 5288-5299). The proof (lines 5301-5351) is a genuine four-beat argument: the property-(I) assembly of the transformation, the reduction to the filtered quotients through the Rlim computation with split transition maps, an induction on the filtration through the induced maps of short exact sequences, and the final reduction to the dual map via products of shifts of the B-dual and exactness of the dual. H2: the individual lemmas are standard, but the induction structure and the two reduction steps carry the proof and no step is a bare citation.
